title: Rules engine: pure functions + variant config, property-tested
description: Pure Elixir: board topology, legal_moves/2, apply_move/3, throw scoring from the variant table, turn/extra-throw sequencing, captures, win detection. Throw value is an INPUT (rules contain no RNG). Separate audited RNG module drawing outcomes with chi-square fairness test over large samples. Property tests (no illegal states reachable, conservation of pieces, termination via simulated playthroughs) and mass random-game simulation as gates. Variant behavior entirely via config struct.
notes:
Assumed variant chosen (owner ruling: common rules, pending chopaat-tbc): 6-cowrie Pachisi/Chopat table per Masters of Games (best-documented complete ruleset). Values by mouths-up: 2..5 -> face value; 6 -> 6+grace; 1 -> 10+grace; 0 -> 25+grace. Grace = extra throw + permits entry from Charkoni (first piece enters on any throw). Board 4 arms x 3 cols x 8; 12 castles (arm-end middle + 4th-from-end in each outer column); path 84 steps (down own middle, anticlockwise circuit, up own middle, exact throw into Charkoni). 4 pieces/player, capture all enemy on non-castle landing (+extra throw), cannot land on enemy-held castle, own stacking ok, no blockades, free-for-all win (first all-4 home). 7-cowrie Wikipedia Chaupar table + partnership play + capture-before-home recorded as alternatives in decisions/2026-08-30-assumed-variant.md. All choices are Chopaat.Variant fields.
SCOPE CHANGE: owner delivered authoritative RULESET.md (Gujarat variation) on master; assumed-common-variant research discarded. Revised plan: Variant struct keeps family-config architecture with :gujarat defaults verbatim (7 shells; table 0up=7,1=11,2=2,3=3,4=4,5=25,6=30,7up=14; specials 7/11/14/25/30 extra roll; entry 11/25/30; bonus steps when base empty; N%3 triple-repeat cancellation; capture=one extra turn; gate/tod/khadu incl. both coordinate transforms; row-6 marker; total-roll finishing accounting; placement finish, last player loses; 4p home 83/connector 75/gate 54, 6p 117/109/71; gandi + 2v2 deferred as flags). Engine models a TURN explicitly: roll-collection phase (chain until non-special) then assignment phase (atomic rolls assigned one at a time, legality recomputed per assignment; forced khadus preempt and burn dana/pagdu). Rules expose could_enter?/had_legal_move? facts + per-player drought counters for the RNG-assist layer; RNG draws shell configs with 0.5 or 0.7 up-bias, chi-square vs Binomial(7,.5) and (7,.7). All RULESET.md worked examples (khadu 72+25->25, 76+25->29, 54+30->12, 75+11->14; position-73 accounting cases) become verbatim example tests. Formalization ambiguities collected for owner (finishing-khadu +15 conditionality, unlock consumes roll, burn ordering vs assignable lower rolls, bonus-step timing, freeze scope, blocked khadu landings) — recorded in decisions/ + final report, resolution by editing RULESET.md.
Rules engine landed on feat/rules-engine (d868a52, pushed). Implements RULESET.md (Gujarat) verbatim as default :gujarat Variant. Modules: Chopaat.{Variant,Board,Pawn,Throw,Rules,Game,RNG}. Board shares the asset lane's absolute cell addressing (cell_t{track}_l{lane}_r{row}) with position->cell mapping + doctests. Gates all green: format, credo --strict (ex_slop+jump active, 0 issues), warnings-as-errors, mix test 102 passing (7 doctests, 4 properties, 91 tests) incl. all RULESET worked examples verbatim, 1800 simulated games/run (1500x4p mean 804 events/271 turns, 300x6p mean 1818 events/605 turns, all terminate with full placements, captures>=players-1 each), chi-square RNG fairness Binomial(7,.5)+Binomial(7,.7)+128-config uniformity. 10 formalization interpretations + owner questions recorded in decisions/2026-08-30-gujarat-formalization.md — resolution by editing RULESET.md (notably: finishing-khadu +15 conditional on passing the connector; unlock consumes the roll; forced-khadu preemption/burn ordering). gandi/teams flags present, unimplemented per deferral.

title: Capture the house-rules variant table from the game owner
description: BLOCKING INPUT, cheap but critical: one written page from the owner covering shell count (how many cowries thrown), the value table (apertures-up counts to move values, incl. any special all-up/all-down values), extra-throw triggers, capture rules and safe squares, home-column entry conditions, stacking/blocking rules, and win condition. Becomes the variant config struct + the acceptance oracle for the rules engine. Do NOT let rules-engine work guess these and property-test the guess into concrete.
notes:
Owner ruling (Kevin, 2026-08-30): assume COMMON rules to get rolling — the rules lane researches documented Chaupar/Chopaat variants, records the chosen assumption as a decision file + variant config struct, and proceeds. This bead stays open as the owner-confirmation gate: when the friend's written table arrives, diff it against the assumed config (config-only change by design). chopaat-y14 is unblocked by this ruling.
RESOLVED: owner delivered the authoritative ruleset — committed as RULESET.md on master (the Gujarat variation, now the default :gujarat variant). Far richer than any documented common variant: 7 shells with score table {0→7, 1→11, 2→2, 3→3, 4→4, 5→25, 6→30, 7→14}; extra rolls on specials; extra turn on capture; bonus steps; triple-repeat cancellation (N%3); gate/tod/khadu system with two distinct khadu coordinate transforms; drought-based 70/30 shell bias per player; 4- and 6-player boards (83/117 positions); placement finish order. Mad pawn (gandi) and 2v2 explicitly deferred. RULESET.md is the acceptance oracle; TBDs get resolved by editing the file, not chat.

title: Per-turn camera orbit: each player views the board from their seat
description: OWNER FEATURE (2026-08-31): on each turn change, the 3D camera moves so the active player views their own part of the board — their home arm at the bottom of the screen, natural pass-and-play perspective. Design: eased orbit around the board center on {:turn_passed} (and at game start for seat 0), preserving the tuned elevation/distance from Scene.rig/1; 90-degree steps for 4p, 60 for 6p; shortest-arc direction; ~800ms ease-in-out via the existing 30Hz tick pattern (Scene.Move precedent) driving per-frame camera patches — no new plugin surface required (mob_scene3d-c60's framing helpers are an optional later upgrade, do not block on it). Sequencing details: orbit runs AFTER the handoff prompt is confirmed (the new player is holding the phone), completes before input unlocks; bot turns orbit too at spectate pacing (it reads well in auto mode); throw/tumble camera stays the orbited frame (the tumble entry is out-of-frame at ALL orbit angles — VERIFY against the re-baked entry margins for the four/six seat angles; if a seat angle breaks the out-of-frame guarantee, note it for a tumble re-bake rather than hacking the camera). 2D mode: unaffected for now (rotating the 2D cross is a separate owner question — note it on the bead when landing). Tests: ScreenCase coverage for orbit state transitions + input gating; device verification with a recording of two consecutive turn handoffs (the orbit IS motion — recording, not stills); scene/1 readback asserts final camera transforms per seat. Gates per AGENTS.md.
notes: LANDED on branch feat/camera-orbit (worktree /Users/kevin/code/worktrees/chopaat-orbit), HEAD 9179d15, pushed to GenericJam/chopaat. Design: Chopaat.Scene.Orbit (pure eased yaw state, Scene.Move 30Hz tick pattern, shortest arc, smoothstep, 800ms, seat_yaw = seat*360/n); Scene.rig/2 takes :camera_yaw, composes q_y(yaw)*q_x(-52) directly (from_euler X*Y*Z would roll the horizon); GameScreen: orbit starts on handoff_done confirm (never before — the prompt holds the outgoing frame), input (throw/action/pick) locked while orbit in flight, bot turn_passed orbits immediately (runner cadence = spectate pacing), extra turns keep the frame, 2D snaps yaw silently, mode-toggle/rematch snap. ENTRY-MARGIN VERDICT: baked entry stays out-of-frame at ALL seat yaws — gate.mjs now sweeps 4p 0/90/180/270 and 6p 0/60..300 when re-deriving spawn keyframes from the GLB; min margin ratios (threshold 1.0, bake margin was 1.08): 4p worst 1.46 (yaw 180), 6p worst 1.14 (yaw 240) — NO re-bake needed; the check is durable in the asset gate. NOTE (bake-time nuance): the exporter decimates the constant-velocity entry to endpoint keyframes, so any tooling must sample by time, not keyframe index. Tests: 334 passing (was 314): Orbit unit suite (scene_orbit_test.exs), Scene camera-rig suite (all seat yaws, no roll, exact yaw-0 == original rig), ScreenCase orbit suite (handoff-then-orbit sequencing, input gating, bot orbit, extra-turn no-op, rematch snap, 2D snap, mode-toggle drop). Device evidence (scripts/device_orbit_evidence.exs): pool emulator 5821 AND physical Moto — native scene/1 camera world_transform matches Scene.build at every seat yaw (pos/basis delta 0.0) for 4p and 6p incl. the 270->0 wrap, orbit observed mid-swing (~18 samples per handoff), throws settle clean under orbited cameras; recording of two consecutive handoffs with orbit on the physical Moto: evidence/android_moto_orbit_handoffs.mp4 + logs evidence/android_moto_orbit.log, android_emu_orbit.log. Gates: format/credo --strict/compile --warnings-as-errors/full tests/asset gate all green. OWNER QUESTION (per spec, noting on landing): 2D mode is unaffected — should the 2D cross rotate per seat too? Separate decision. Plugin finding filed: mob_scene3d-10z (full-size screenrecord shows scene3d SurfaceView black on redroid with current native; --size capture works; physical device fine).

title: Cloth board skin: woven texture + wrinkles (asset round 3)
description: OWNER RULING (2026-08-31): the board is cloth — skin it to LOOK like cloth, and 'wrinkles in the cloth would really sell it.' Approach: keep the approved dark palette; add (1) a woven-fabric base-color + roughness texture (subtle, dark, thread-scale), (2) baked wrinkle NORMAL MAP — soft irregular folds from a Blender cloth sim or sculpt, baked to normals so geometry stays cheap (tri budget unchanged), stronger toward edges/between arms, gentle under the play field so markings stay flat-legible; optionally very low-amplitude displacement on the cloth ground only. Constraints: cell markings/safe/gate/center must remain crisply legible over the wrinkles (markings can sit on flatter panels, or bake wrinkles to avoid marking zones); textures embedded in the glb (renders today, no plugin change; KTX2 via the pipeline if size demands); node addressing contract unchanged (gate asserts); both player counts. Evidence: contact sheet at the game camera light+dark, plus one close-up render showing the wrinkle normals catching the light — that is the shot that sells it.
notes: DONE (feat/assets-round3). Cloth skin per ruling, geometry budgets unchanged: (1) 256px plain-weave baseColor+roughness tile (2mm thread pitch, approved dark palette baked in) tiled ~30x via second planar UV layer TEXCOORD_1 + core-glTF REPEAT sampler (deliberately NO KHR_texture_transform - no new plugin surface); (2) 1024px baked wrinkle NORMAL MAP on TEXCOORD_0 — scripted-sculpt height field (fold ridges + billow), strong within ~35mm of outline edges + boosted at arm-shoulder crotches, floored 0.28 under the play field; markings legible BY CONSTRUCTION (tiles are separate rigid meshes; only board_cloth carries the normals). TANGENTs exported (slab triangulated for MikkTSpace). Chose scripted sculpt over cloth sim for headless determinism + direct amplitude control (decision record). Sizes: board.glb 788KB / board_6p.glb 1.15MB embedded PNG — under the new 2MB maxFileKB gate budget, KTX2 not needed (gate enforces the trigger). Node contract untouched, gate green. Evidence: board_light/dark, THE SELLING SHOT assets/contact_sheets/cloth_closeup.png (raking 9-deg warm key across the arm margin, folds catching light). Integration lane: first device run should eyeball TEXCOORD_1 sampling + tangent-space normals through the plugin renderer (embedded textures already render; only core glTF used).

title: Throw presentation v1: shells drop in from out-of-frame; future shake-and-spill seam
description: OWNER RULING (2026-08-31): the current falling-onto-the-center-square animation look is APPROVED. V1 presentation: shells enter from out of frame (top) and land on the center plate — re-bake or extend the tumble takes so entry starts above the camera frustum (the baking script's drop height + camera framing are parameters; verify entry is out-of-frame at the ACTUAL game camera for both player counts). LEAVE ROOM FOR CHANGE: put the throw presentation behind a small module boundary (ThrowPresentation: choose take + entry style per throw) so later variants swap in without touching game or session code. FUTURE (recorded, not built): cinematic shake-to-throw — player shakes the phone (accelerometer; would need a mob sensor surface — file the mob bead when promoted) and the shells SPILL ACROSS THE BOARD/screen (wider scatter sim variant, possibly settling across arm cells, then gathering to the plate or scoring in place — owner to rule when promoted). The manifest contract (outcome + per-slot orientations) is invariant across all presentation variants.
notes: RE-BAKE HALF DONE (feat/assets-round3); the ThrowPresentation module seam + future shake-and-spill stay with the app lanes (this split recorded per the round-3 plan). Shells now ENTER FROM OUT OF FRAME (top) at the ACTUAL game camera, both player counts: rig framing read from lib/chopaat/scene.ex rig/1 (READ-ONLY) and mirrored as GAME_CAMERAS in tumble.py (4p cam (0,1.05,0.78), 6p (0,1.2,0.9), pitch -52, fov_y 45; keep in sync). HONEST HIGH-ENERGY BAKES WERE PILOTED AND REJECTED: real 0.72-0.87m drops arrive 2.2-3.9 m/s, Bullet exposes no rolling friction, shells rolled off-plate >95% across three tunings (0-1 accepts / 240 sims each); ballistics forbids slow arrival from a high start. Shipped: the sim is the UNCHANGED approved round-2 throw + a baked entry prepended per shell, built backward from the launch state (constant tumble, ~3 m/s descent easing into the exact launch velocity over 8 frames — C1-continuous splice), walked above the top frustum plane of BOTH cameras with 8% tan margin (+2 frames); out-of-frame hold pads the 7 shells to one frame range. Same manifest contract + classification rigor: 32 takes / 232 sims, durations 1.50-2.48s (band kept, entry included). Manifest gains entry section (cameras/clearance/margin/fall). Verified 3 ways: (1) tumble.py asserts frames 1-2 of every shell out-of-frame at both cameras; (2) gate.mjs re-derives every slot's FIRST translation keyframe from the GLB binary and asserts it above both frusta; (3) ACCEPTANCE RENDERS assets/contact_sheets/tumble_entry_{4p,6p}.png — 8 outcomes x 6 frames AT the game cameras (360x400 game aspect): frame-1 tiles are pixel-identical board-only (no shells), stream enters from the top edge, settles on plate. tumbles.glb 875KB after resample.

title: Authentic pawns: two-tone painted turned wood, per-player colors (asset round 3)

Expected shape of the answer: turned-wood profile with painted body in the player color + contrasting band/tip (often ivory/natural wood or a second accent), visible wood grain under the paint (subtle roughness/grain texture, embedded in the glb — embedded glTF textures already render through the plugin). STRUCTURAL CHANGE: the current pawn is one mesh/one neutral material tinted at runtime; two-tone needs TWO named materials (body + accent) both addressable by the runtime override path — coordinate with GameScreen's tint code (it targets the material by name; update together). Need distinct, colorblind-checked player palettes for 4 AND 6 players (6 needs six distinguishable colors on a dark board — verify against the dark cloth via contact sheet). Deliver via the scripted pipeline + one contact-sheet round: pawn variants upright/tipped/upside-down on the dark board, per palette.
notes:
ASSET HALF DONE (feat/assets-round3). Reference research + URLs in decisions/2026-08-31-assets-round3.md: traditional chaupar/pachisi pawns are lathe-turned BEEHIVE pieces (squat domed body, turned collar bead, small dome cap), Channapatna lac-turnery gloss, two-tone = player-color body + natural/ivory band+tip. pawn.py rewritten to that profile (44mm x 26mm, 1464 tris, directional +X nose kept — poses read at 45 deg); TWO named materials pawn_body (near-white, tintable) + pawn_accent (authored ivory, never tinted); 256px wood-grain baseColor+roughness embedded (104 KB). Palettes: assets/palettes.json (Okabe-Ito; 4p verm/green/yellow/skyblue, 6p + blue/purple; linear_rgba = the factor values for the Setup tint follow-up). Colorblind-verified: Machado-2009 severity-1.0 deutan/protan sims in linear RGB, min pairwise CIE76 dE asserted >=10 (4p worst 33.6, 6p worst 17.9), sheets pawns_{4p,6p}{,_deutan,_protan}.png on the dark board + palette_cvd_report.txt.

EXACT RUNTIME CHANGE REQUIRED (follow-up after both lanes merge — NOT in the asset lane): Chopaat.Scene.pawn_entities/6 (+ target_* markers + selected emissive) set Model.material = %Material{base_color: tint}; the plugin's applyMaterial (MobScene3dBridge.kt) applies the override to EVERY materialInstance, so the ivory pawn_accent would take the player color too. Needs (1) mob_scene3d: name-scoped material override (e.g. Model.materials %{"pawn_body" => %Material{}} or Material.target field; native filters materialInstances by glTF material name) — plugin gap, file bead in mob_scene3d tracker; (2) chopaat: scope the pawn tint/emissive to "pawn_body". Until then runtime tints both materials (round-2 look); asset renders correctly today.
MERGED after coordinator review (pawn sheets + cloth closeup + CVD report eyeballed; gate re-verified by agent, 21 GLBs green). ON-DEVICE CAVEAT until mob_scene3d-bqc + tint scoping land: whole-model tint colors the ivory accent too, so pawns render fully player-colored (round-2 look); the authentic two-tone appears once the name-scoped override ships. title: Machine-playable game API: the interface an LLM (or any external agent) could play through
description: Owner directive (2026-08-31): expose the game so an LLM agent COULD play it — essentially an API, the agent-legibility principle applied to gameplay. Design: a documented machine client protocol over the session boundary — observe(game) returns the full public state as plain data (board occupancy by cell address, pawn states incl. tipped/jammed/home, pending rolls + phase, tod/gate/assist facts, placements); legal_actions(game, seat) returns the exact action terms the session accepts; act(game, seat, action) submits and returns the resulting events. Shape it JSON-serializable end to end (atoms whitelisted) so the same protocol rides Erlang dist today and HTTP/MCP later without redesign — but build NO server now (possible-not-built, per the presentation-is-a-client ruling). Include a protocol doc (guides/machine-play.md) written FOR an agent reader: state schema, action grammar, the two-phase turn, khadu semantics, worked turn examples. Acceptance: a scripted external client (plain escript/exs over dist — no UI modules imported) plays a complete 4p game via the API only, and the existing random bot is REIMPLEMENTED on top of this same API to prove bots and external agents use one interface. This doubles as the session boundary's integration test. Depends on chopaat-uzu.
notes:
Verification model (owner, 2026-08-31): agents can play via this API (logic plane) OR via the phone interface with Mob.Test tap/pick + scene readback (full-stack plane). The strongest test uses BOTH on one game: drive through the UI, assert through observe/1 — the API is the oracle for UI-driven games, so any state divergence is a presentation bug by construction. Ship a dual-drive helper with this bead (drive_ui + assert_api on the same session) for the acceptance suites to reuse.
Protocol version/stability policy (decision, 2026-08-31): Chopaat.MachinePlay carries its own semver, independent of the app — v1.0.0 shipped on feat/machine-play (11978b0). Within a major version the wire surface is APPEND-ONLY: new state fields, action types, event types, and error reasons may be added (minor bump); nothing is renamed, removed, or retyped without a major bump; clients must ignore unknown fields and unknown event types (decode_action ignores unknown extra fields for the same reason). describe/0 returns the whole contract as data and its 'version' key is the runtime source of truth. Wire conventions fixed at 1.0.0: server->client is atom-keyed plain data that the stdlib JSON encoder maps canonically (atoms->strings, nil->null); client->server actions are string-keyed post-JSON-decode maps, returned by legal_actions verbatim-resendable; the khadu commit is its own action type confirm_khadu (the name is the confirmation — assign can never commit one). Transport-agnostic by construction: same maps over in-BEAM calls, Erlang dist (scripts/machine_client.exs proves it from a node with no game code loaded), and HTTP/MCP later — no server built, per the possible-not-built ruling. Dual-drive helper shipped: test/support/dual_drive.ex (drive_ui + assert_api, MachinePlay.observe as the UI oracle), reusable for chopaat-4nn. Gates green, 314 tests (+20).

title: Session boundary: extract the game into a presentation-agnostic session process
description: Owner ruling (AGENTS.md 'Presentation is a client', 2026-08-31): the game must be hostable without any renderer. Today the GameScreen holds Game state in its own assigns — the screen IS the host. Extract: Chopaat.Session (GenServer or equivalent) owning Game state + Chopaat.RNG + cosmetic seed + variant + player config, exposing a client API (join/observe, throw, assign_action, confirm_khadu, state subscription as pure data — events out, commands in). Screens become clients: GameScreen subscribes and renders; every existing ScreenCase test keeps passing with the screen refactored to consume the session. HARD RULE enforced by a test: no module under Chopaat.{Game,Rules,Board,Variant,Session} references Mob.*, scene, or screen modules (a compile-time boundary check — assert on module attributes or xref). This is the seam that makes the 2D client, a projected-server web client, and LAN/online all possible without touching game code. Sequence AFTER chopaat-hre merges (do not yank the running integration lane); the 2D epic builds on this.
notes:
API shape decision (session boundary, feat/session-boundary lane) — recorded early for the 27z/85o/u8x lanes:

Chopaat.Session (GenServer). Commands in, events out, all plain data; RNG lives server-side.
  start_link(opts)  # :setup (Chopaat.Setup) | :players/:names/:variant, :rng_seed, :game (fixture state), :draw (shells-draw injection, test seam), :name
  new_game(session, opts)          # rematch: fresh Game, same seats; emits {:game_started, ...}
  observe(session)                 # full public state, strictly JSON-serializable (whitelisted atoms; occupancy keyed by cell-name strings; per-seat pawn states incl tipped/jammed/bypass/home; phase+rolls/pending/bonus; tod/gate/assist+drought facts; placements; board geometry facts; seq)
  game(session) / setup(session)   # %Chopaat.Game{}/%Chopaat.Setup{} snapshots — in-BEAM renderer convenience (clients MAY depend on game modules; never the reverse)
  export(session)                  # %{game, rng, setup, seq} — diagnostics/persistence/predictors (device scripts)
  legal_actions(session, seat)     # exact Rules.action() terms the session accepts ([] off-turn / outside :assigning)
  throw(session, seat)             # SESSION draws shells (fair or drought-assisted) + a cosmetic uniform int, applies {:roll, shells}, returns {:ok, events}
  assign(session, seat, action)    # non-khadu actions; khadu here => {:error, :khadu_requires_confirmation} (destructive commit is explicit at the API level)
  confirm_khadu(session, seat, {:khadu, i, ix})
  subscribe/unsubscribe            # events as {:chopaat_session, session_pid, seq, event}, seq strictly increasing

Event vocabulary (designed for renderers; decision record decisions/2026-08-31-session-boundary.md):
  {:throw_result, %{seat, shells, up_count, score, special, entry, cosmetic, phase, rolls, pending, bonus_steps}}
  {:moved, %{seat, pawn, action, roll, from, to, path}}   # positions as %{state,track,cell-name} maps; path drives hop animations / 2D redraw
  {:captured, %{seat, victim_seat, victim_pawn, cell, tod_earned, victim_tod_lost}}
  {:khadu, %{seat, pawn, roll, burned: %{dana: [...], pagdu: n}}}
  {:wasted, %{seat, roll | :bonus}}
  {:turn_passed, %{seat, next_seat, extra_turn}}
  {:placement, %{seat, rank}} · {:game_over, %{placements, loser}} · {:game_started, %{...}}

Throw pacing: presentation grace, not dependency — the session advances the moment the command lands; no presentation ack exists. Clients present at their own pace (the 3D screen holds the observed state until its tumble settles; a headless client ignores cosmetics entirely). The cosmetic field is a server-drawn uniform int; renderers map it onto their take library (rem/length) so 3D and 2D present the identical outcome deterministically. Chopaat.Throws shrinks to a presentation-side performance boundary: perform(up_count, cosmetic) + schedule_done + settle_check (settle verification stays client-side: it verifies the RENDERER against the session truth — the two-plane model).
Implementation complete on branch feat/session-boundary (HEAD a9d2c03, pushed to origin; worktree /Users/kevin/code/worktrees/chopaat-session). Master untouched.

DELIVERED:
- lib/chopaat/session.ex — Chopaat.Session GenServer per the API-shape note above (commands return {:ok, events} AND broadcast to subscribers as {:chopaat_session, pid, seq, event}, broadcast-before-reply, seq strictly increasing; khadu via assign/3 -> {:error, :khadu_requires_confirmation}).
- Throws refactor: outcome decided in the session (shells + cosmetic int); Chopaat.Throws = perform(up_count, cosmetic)/schedule_done/settle_check only. Deterministic take pick via rem(cosmetic, takes). Session.export/1 + Session.draw_throw/2 replay the exact server draw for host-side predictors (device_acceptance.exs updated accordingly).
- GameScreen = pure client: subscribes, renders from observed state + events, commands via taps; presented state adopts the session truth on tumble settle (presentation grace); move performances follow the :moved event path; settle verification stays client-side (renderer vs session truth).
- Boundary test test/chopaat/boundary_test.exs: BEAM :atoms chunk (catches struct-literal refs — proven: it sees Mob.Scene3d.IR.Animation in Throws.Baked) + transitive :imports walk. Game plane Chopaat.{Game,Rules,Board,Variant,Throw,Pawn,RNG,Session,Setup} verified clean; build fails loudly on violation.
- Tests 191 -> 220 (all pass): all prior ScreenCase behavior preserved driving through the session (drive/pump helpers; scripted outcomes via session :draw seam, test/support/scripted_dice.ex); new session_test.exs (headless 4p+6p full games, concurrent observers, event ordering/seq, JSON round-trip of observe/1, command validation, khadu-confirm, drought-bias-through-session, export determinism).
- Gates: mix format / credo --strict / compile --warnings-as-errors / mix test all green; asset gate (gate.mjs) exit 0, 21 GLBs + shell_pool + tumble_manifest PASS.
- Device sanity (pool emulator 127.0.0.1:5821, node chopaat_uzu1): scripted short game on the refactored screen — 4 throws settled + natively readback-verified clean (ok=4, 0 mismatch/skip/error), 2 assignment moves, 1 native move-readback matching session pose. Evidence committed: evidence/session_sanity.log + evidence/session_sanity_board.png (mid-game board, Player 3 assigning). Full matrix re-runs at chopaat-4nn.
- Decision record: decisions/2026-08-31-session-boundary.md (event vocabulary table, throw-pacing ruling, boundary-test mechanics, session lifetime).

Unblocks 27z (bots consume this client API), 85o (protocol doc formalizes observe/events — do NOT redesign, serialize), u8x (2D client builds against observe/1 cell names + events).

title: AI opponents: single-player against bots
description: The biggest playability multiplier: Rules.legal_actions/1 + the pure reducer make bots trivial to host. Tier 1: a legal-random bot (proves the loop). Tier 2: heuristic bot (prefer captures > entering > advancing the leader > safe-cell stops; avoid parking before an active gate; khadu-choice heuristic picks the least-bad pawn). Bot turns run through the SAME turn flow with visible throws/moves (short delays so humans can follow). Mix human/bot seats freely in the menu (4p or 6p). Mass bot-vs-bot simulation already exists in tests — reuse it to sanity-check the heuristic wins more than random. NO cheating: bots see exactly the public game state.
notes:
Owner directive (2026-08-31): initial setup is COMPUTER-PLAYS-ITSELF — an
auto mode where every seat is a basic (non-LLM) bot and the game runs
unattended: menu gains 'Auto' (all-bot seats, 4p or 6p), turns advance on a

title: 2D board mode: the always-playable ground truth
description: Owner directive: a fully playable 2D presentation of the same game so people can ALWAYS play, everywhere, regardless of 3D support — and it doubles as the debugging view and the accessibility mode. Same Chopaat.Game reducer, same screens/HUD (the two-phase turn structure, khadu confirm, handoff are presentation-agnostic and already built); only the board viewport swaps: a pure Mob-UI 2D board (grid/canvas rendering of arms/lanes/rows with the same cell addressing, tinted pawn markers, safe/gate/center markings mirroring the dark board's visual language) and a 2D throw presentation (seven shell glyphs flipping to the drawn configuration — no physics needed, the manifest's aperture arrays make the 2D result IDENTICAL to what 3D shows). Mode toggle in settings + per-device persistence; default 2D when the scene3d viewport reports unsupported. Acceptance: full game playable in 2D on both platforms with zero scene3d involvement; toggling mid-game preserves state (same assigns).
notes:
Owner ruling refinement (2026-08-31): the 2D mode is a CLIENT of the session boundary (new bead: session extraction), deliberately canvas-grade simple — Mob.Canvas or a plain grid of primitives, chosen for verifiability over beauty: it is the debugging surface (a human or agent should be able to eyeball/readback the entire game state from it at a glance) as well as the always-playable fallback. Do not build it against screen-held state; build it against the session API.
Rendering choice (2D board): plain grid of Mob primitives (tappable :box cells + tinted disc boxes), NOT Mob.Canvas. Why: Mob.UI.canvas/1 strips props to width/height/draw — no per-element tap targets, so canvas interaction would need raw coordinate hit-testing that Mob.Test cannot drive by tag. Boxes carry on_tap tags (addressable by test tooling + humans), assert cleanly in ScreenCase, and honor borders/backgrounds — verifiability over beauty, and the tap tags double as the machine-driving surface. 4p lays out as the cross (19x19 slot grid, arms t0 S / t1 E / t2 N / t3 W, CCW, lane 0 on the CCW side per Board docs); 6p uses a flat six-strip layout (arms side by side, center home bar on top) since 60-degree arms cannot be boxed — legibility over geometric fidelity, same cell addressing either way.
Core executed on feat/2d-client (HEAD 268365c, pushed). Board2D (Chopaat.Screens.Board2D): pure Session.observe/1 -> node tree; 4p cross / 6p flat strips; cell ids ARE cell addresses; safe blue / gate ochre (solid active, ring when tod held) / center gold / owner-tinted middle lanes; pawns = tinted discs with stack/tipped(▸)/jammed(✕) glyphs; 7 shell glyph discs flip instantly to the drawn configuration (identical to 3D by manifest). Interaction: {:cell2d,name} select + stack-cycling, {:pawn2d,ix} base pads, targets reuse the tray {:action,action} message so khadu goes through the SAME confirm dialog. GameScreen mode swap (only the board viewport changes), mid-game toggle preserves session+state (ScreenCase + on-device proof), fallback to 2D with one-line notice when Mob.Scene3d.caps/0 says nif_not_loaded (menu defaults 2D there too), debug toggle = cell addresses + seq/phase/turn/last-event readout. Tests: 33 new (board_2d_test 14, game_screen_2d_test 13, settings/menu 3, +existing suites pinned to :scene3d_support seam) — 253 total green; format/credo --strict/compile --warnings-as-errors clean. Device: scripts/device_2d_acceptance.exs green on Android pool emu 5822 (10 throws/6 moves all-2D, presented==observe every batch, toggle round trip on device) and iOS pool sim pool-ios-0 (10 throws/7 moves); evidence/{android_emu_2d_*,ios_sim_2d_*}. Decision record decisions/2026-08-31-2d-board-grid-of-boxes.md. NOT done: per-device persistence of the mode (menu-held only); physical-phone pass-and-play remains the game-level final acceptance.
Core MERGED (post-merge suite green with round-3 assets + session boundary combined). Epic closes: mid-game 2D↔3D toggle preserving the same session pid verified on device — the boundary's acceptance proof delivered. Grid-of-boxes over canvas ruled for agent-legibility (canvas has no tap targets — decision record). Remaining follow-up folded into chopaat-1o6: persist the mode preference per device.

title: Device acceptance: full pass-and-play game on two physical phones
description: The v1 definition of done: a complete game played to completion pass-and-play on the physical Android and iPhone, no terminal involvement, with recordings kept as evidence. Includes a churn soak (many throws/moves) watching frame-time readback and component reclamation. Feel/polish findings from this run become follow-up beads rather than blocking v1.
notes: Device-pool observation (from chopaat-4g7 device work, 2026-08-31 evening): the physical Moto (ZY22DP6HFL) mob.connect refusal was NOT a dist bug on the node — the adb reverse tcp:4369 had been lost, so the app logged 'no EPMD on port 4369 after 10s — skipping dist'. Restoring 'adb -s ZY22DP6HFL reverse tcp:4369 tcp:4369' and restarting the app brought dist up immediately. Second trap: launching the app via monkey/launcher intent (instead of the deploy restart) loses MOB_NODE_SUFFIX/MOB_DIST_PORT extras — the node comes up as plain chopaat@127.0.0.1 on port 9100, so the expected suffixed name never registers; forward tcp:9100 and connect to the plain name, or restart via mix mob.deploy. Also hit on the pool emulator: stale adb forward left tcp:9533 mapped while the fresh deploy pinned 9761 — 'adb forward tcp:9761 tcp:9761' required before Node.connect.

title: Integration: pick-to-move, throw sequencing, camera, scene readback assertions
description: Wire rules to scene: tap piece (Scene3d pick) -> legal-move highlighting -> confirm -> animated move; throw button -> RNG draw -> matching tumble animation -> {:animation_done} -> post-settle scene readback asserting shell orientations match the drawn value -> rules apply. Camera framing for the board (static or gentle orbit — decide with owner). Device-driven acceptance via Mob.Test + Scene3d introspection. Depends on mob_scene3d picking (mob_scene3d-na8) and introspection (mob_scene3d-0n7).
notes:
From RULESET.md visual notes + rules: (1) a pawn in the final stretch is displayed TIPPED ON ITS SIDE as a status marker, and must flip back upright if it commits a finishing khadu (it leaves the stretch); (2) upside-down is reserved for the future mad pawn (deferred) — do not use it for anything else; (3) the throw UI must support the extra-roll chain (player manually throws again after each special until a non-special lands, THEN assignment begins — collection phase and assignment phase are distinct in the UI just as in the engine); (4) khadu commits need a clear confirm flow since they burn pending dana/pagdu (2/3/4 rolls + bonus steps) — that is a destructive choice the player must see coming.
Animation playback MERGED upstream (mob_scene3d master): %Animation{name, play_id, loop, speed, paused, seek}; on_animation_done: tag (default delivers {:animation_done, play_id}, at most once per play_id); scene/1 exposes animation_state + per-node world transforms (the settle-readback surface — the k4 contract was verified on 3 devices upstream using tumble.py's own classifier). Integration can wire the real throw sequencing now: screens' Throws boundary → set animation with new play_id → await done → scene readback → assert vs manifest → Game reducer applies.

title: Cowrie tumble animation library (baked physics, outcome-sorted)
description: Blender headless rigid-body sims: drop N shells with randomized impulses, simulate, read final aperture orientations back in-script, bake to keyframes, export as named glTF animations sorted by outcome count (several takes per outcome so throws do not look canned). The outcome-classification step is asserted in the generation script, not eyeballed. Depends on the shell model and on mob_scene3d animation playback (mob_scene3d-al6 — named animation selection, completion events, post-settle orientation readback).
notes:
RULESET.md (Gujarat variation) is authoritative: exactly 7 shells per throw, outcomes 0-7 apertures up (score table in the ruleset). Bake several takes per outcome count 0..7. The drought-assistance bias (70/30) only changes outcome FREQUENCY, never the animations — no extra takes needed for it.
Design constraint from the owner's shell ruling: throws use 7 DISTINCT shell models drawn per game from the variant pool. Therefore bake tumble MOTION per outcome against a canonical collision proxy (variants share ~0.023-0.024m bounds, budget-enforced) targeting slots shell_0..shell_6; the visual mesh per slot is assigned at runtime per game. Do NOT bake per-variant animations — combinatorial explosion. Verify the proxy hull is a fair stand-in for all pool variants (same rest orientations).
feat/tumble-library (2204504) delivers the library. 32 animations throw_k{0..7}_v{0..3} (4 takes per outcome) in ONE priv/assets/tumbles.glb (613 KB after resample --tolerance 0.001): slots share the node set + placeholder proxy mesh and animations are transform-only (~10-25 KB each), so per-outcome files would only complicate the runtime contract. Canonical proxy = convex hull at pool-mean dims (0.0235x0.0166x0.0106 m), fairness vs the pool envelope asserted + recorded in assets/tumble_manifest.json. Classification robustness: 160 sims for 32 accepted takes (128 re-rolls: 40 outcome!=target, 25 settle-band, 55 off-plate, 15 ambiguous side-rest). gate.mjs gateTumbles() re-derives every final quaternion from the GLB binary and cross-checks the manifest (tamper-tested). Paid-for physics in decisions/2026-08-30-tumble-library.md: Bullet 0.04 m default margin > shell size; object origin = CoM (sim on centroid-origin clone, keyframes re-based to center-bottom); animated-kinematic launch keyframes make bodies sleep-ineligible + no rolling friction, so takes end via stability window + 0.4 s tail convergence onto the final simulated pose. Previews: assets/contact_sheets/tumble_throw_{k0_v0,k4_v0,k7_v0}.mp4 (Blender 5.x dropped FFMPEG render — PNG + system ffmpeg). Gates: gate.mjs 23 PASS exit 0; mix format/credo/compile/test green (102 tests).
MERGED after independent gate re-run (23 PASS incl. quaternion re-derivation cross-check). tumbles.glb 613KB, 32 animations (4 takes x outcomes 0-7), manifest is the runtime contract (per-slot aperture_up arrays for readback assertions). Physics findings documented in decisions/. Previews under assets/contact_sheets/tumble_*.mp4 for the owner. Playback on-device depends on mob_scene3d animation support (al6) — the baking half of this bead is DONE.

Fix is implemented in mob_dev (branch fix/android-ui-components-bootstrap, PR pending): the generated io.mob.plugin.MobPluginBootstrap.registerAll(this) — which MainActivity already calls — now emits com.genericjam.chopaat.MobNativeViewRegistry.register("Mob_Scene3d_Viewport") { props, _send -> io.mob.scene3d.MobScene3dViewport(props) } from the manifest's ui_components (key from ios.view_module fallback, composable qualified by the bridge_class package). Once that mob_dev version is released/updated in chopaat, removal = delete the WORKAROUND block in MainActivity.kt (lines ~152-158) and rebuild with mix mob.deploy --native; MobPluginBootstrap.kt regenerates with the registration. Verified on a fresh mob.new host with mob_scene3d as a path dep: registration appears in generated MobPluginBootstrap.kt with no hand edit. iOS side already worked via IOSBootstrap/mob_register_plugins.
mob_dev 0.6.31 released with the ui_components codegen fix — the workaround at android/.../MainActivity.kt:152-158 is now a pure deletion once chopaat bumps mob_dev to 0.6.31. Fold the bump + deletion into the integration or acceptance lane.
